attack.method: Live re-fetch, this fire, of every citation underlying fire 1's 2 QUALIFYING_RECOMMENDED finds (entries n=1 Mendeley, n=3 IJTSRD/Zenodo) plus 3 genuine-Zenodo comparison entries (n=2, n=4, n=5), checking whether the claimed verbatim quote actually resolves at the claimed source URL/API.
attack.observation: Entry n=3 FIRED the refutation criterion: its citation ('Zenodo REST API record metadata.license field') does not resolve -- the DOI is not a Zenodo record at all, and the Zenodo record id its trailing digits coincide with (15748) is an unrelated paper with a different license (cc-zero, not cc-by-4.0). Entries n=2, n=4, n=5 (genuine 10.5281/zenodo.* DOIs) did NOT fire -- both title and license independently reverified byte-for-byte against a fresh live query.

corrected_qualifying_find_n3.correction_note: Fire 1 (20260812T120001-3712582-97e3beba268d) cited this entry's license as 'Zenodo REST API record metadata.license field returned {"id": "cc-by-4.0"}'. That citation is FALSE: the DOI is an IJTSRD article, never a Zenodo record; the Zenodo record id implied by the DOI's trailing digits (15748) is an unrelated 2014 robotics paper licensed cc-zero. The underlying disposition (CC-BY-4.0, QUALIFYING_RECOMMENDED) happens to be directionally correct once re-grounded in the TRUE source (ijtsrd.com itself, which independently states the CC BY 4.0 grant), but the original citation did not verify what it claimed to verify.

proposed_followups.defect: U-DATA fire 1's citation-verification methodology treated a DOI's trailing numeric suffix as if it were interchangeable with a Zenodo record id without checking the DOI registrant prefix (10.31142 IJTSRD vs 10.5281 Zenodo) -- a reusable failure mode any future data-hunt fire could repeat against any non-Zenodo DOI that happens to end in digits.
proposed_followups.proposed_done_criterion: A future data-hunt or ledger-audit fire adds a mechanical DOI-registrant-prefix check (resolve https://doi.org/<doi> and assert the final host matches the claimed citation system, e.g. zenodo.org for 'Zenodo REST API') to the standard search-record schema/tooling used by this module's U-* data campaign items, so this class of citation defect is caught mechanically rather than requiring a dedicated audit fire.

why: The narrower claim under test this fire -- that fire 1's 2 QUALIFYING_RECOMMENDED acquisition-queue entries were each verified against a real, traceable verbatim license quote from their named source, as the item's own done_criterion requires -- is REFUTED for entry n=3 (DDM/MDA, IJTSRD 10.31142/ijtsrd15748 / acquisition-queue.jsonl line 59). Fire 1 cited 'Zenodo REST API record metadata.license field' for a DOI that is not, and has never been, a Zenodo record; live re-query of the Zenodo record id apparently implied by the DOI's trailing digits returns a wholly unrelated 2014 robotics paper under a DIFFERENT license (cc-zero) than the one fire 1 quoted (cc-by-4.0). This is a genuine citation-provenance defect in a queued acquisition ask, of the same class this module has previously flagged elsewhere (ip-fto claim-chart provenance, source-ledger dual-source/query-traceability). It is corrected here, not merely flagged: the TRUE source (ijtsrd.com itself, fetched live this fire) is independently quoted verbatim, and it confirms the SAME underlying license grant (CC BY 4.0) -- so the disposition (QUALIFYING_RECOMMENDED) is preserved, but now for the right reason. Entries n=1 (Mendeley) and n=2/n=4/n=5 (genuine Zenodo DOIs) were independently re-verified and are NOT corrected; the defect is isolated to entry n=3, not systemic across the 17-source sweep.
